steps.title: Prepare running buffers and stock solutions
steps.instruction: Make all required buffers and protein/compound stocks as described:

substeps.instruction: Add 20 mL of 10× HBS‑EP+ buffer to 180 mL Milli‑Q water to obtain 250 mL HBS‑EP+ running buffer.
Add 25 mL of 10× HBS‑EP+ buffer to 224.975 mL Milli‑Q water, then add 25 µL DMSO to obtain 250 mL HBS‑EP+ running buffer + 0.01 % DMSO.
Add 200 µL DNase‑free water to 100 µg PD‑1 or PD‑L1 protein; vortex and let stand at room temperature for 30 min to dissolve (final concentration 500 µg mL⁻¹, PD‑L1 = 2 000 nM).
Dilute the 500 µg mL⁻¹ PD‑1 stock to 40 µg mL⁻¹ in acetate 5.0 buffer for immobilization.
Prepare 31.25 mM BMS‑1166 stock: dissolve appropriate amount in DMSO (10 µL total).
Prepare 50 mM BMS‑202 stock: dissolve in DMSO (volume as needed).
Prepare NO‑Losartan A stock in DMSO (concentration as required for 0–3 125 nM final dilutions).
Prepare 1 M ethanolamine·HCl (pH 8.5) for deactivation.
Prepare 50 mM NaOH solution for activation wash.
Prepare Glycine 1.5 M (pH 2.5) for regeneration.

steps.title: Immobilize PD‑1 on CM5 sensor chip
steps.instruction: Couple PD‑1 to a CM5 chip by amine coupling using the instrument’s immobilization method.

substeps.instruction: Set SPR instrument temperature to 25 °C, chip type to CM5, and select 1 flow cell per cycle.
Configure flow cell 1 as blank (no ligand) and flow cell 2 for PD‑1 immobilization.
Select “amine coupling” as the method for both flow cells.
Load reagents into the rack:
Tube R2 B1 – 160 µL of 40 µg mL⁻¹ PD‑1 (in acetate 5.0).
Tube R2 B2 – 70 µL of 50 mM NaOH.
Tubes R2 B3 and R2 C3 – 140 µL of ethanolamine (1 M, pH 8.5).
Tubes R2 B4 and R2 C4 – leave empty.
Tubes R2 B5 and R2 C5 – 100 µL of NHS (from amine‑coupling kit).
Tubes R2 B6 and R2 C6 – 100 µL of EDC (from amine‑coupling kit).
Insert the CM5 chip (eject maintenance chip).
Run the following injection sequence:
1. Baseline: inject HBS‑EP+ running buffer.
2. Activate surface: inject 50:50 mixture of EDC + NHS (contact 420 s, flow 10 µL min⁻¹).
3. Baseline buffer injection.
4. Ligand coupling: inject 40 µg mL⁻¹ PD‑1 (contact time as instrument default, flow 10 µL min⁻¹).
5. Deactivate remaining NHS‑esters: inject 1 M ethanolamine·HCl (pH 8.5) (contact 420 s, flow 10 µL min⁻¹).
Observe a slight RU increase after each bulk‑refractive‑index change.
Eject the chip, wash surface with two drops DI water, let dry briefly, and store at 4 °C. Replace running buffer with Milli‑Q water for standby.

steps.title: Validate PD‑1/PD‑L1 interaction (kinetics assay)
steps.instruction: Run a kinetic binding assay of PD‑L1 at multiple concentrations over the immobilized PD‑1 chip.

substeps.instruction: Set instrument method to “PD‑1/PD‑L1 validation”: temperature 25 °C, data collection rate 10 Hz, detection mode “multi”, concentration unit nM.
Assay steps:
Conditioning: 20 replicates.
Startup (conditioning): 10 replicates.
Sample (kinetics): 1 replicate, contact 120 s, dissociation 120 s, flow 10 µL min⁻¹, flow path 1‑4.
Regeneration: inject Glycine 1.5 M, contact 30 s, flow 30 µL min⁻¹, flow path 1‑4.
Carry‑over control: inject 30 s at 40 µL min⁻¹.
Define variables: sample solution, concentration, molecular weight (PD‑L1 MW = 51 300 Da).
Prepare a 96‑well plate:
R1 A1 – 0 nM PD‑L1 (add 100 µL HBS‑EP+).
R1 A2 – 5 nM (2‑fold serial dilution from 10 µL of 40 nM stock).
R1 A3 – 10 nM.
R1 A4 – 20 nM.
R1 A5 – 40 nM.
R1 B1‑B12 – 250 µL Glycine 1.5 M (regeneration).
R1 C1‑C4 – sample buffer (100 µL or 225 µL as indicated).
Seal plate tightly.
Insert the previously immobilized PD‑1 CM5 chip (remove from 4 °C storage).
Place Tube A in HBS‑EP+ + 0.01 % DMSO.
Load the 96‑well plate into the instrument and run the method.
After run, eject chip, insert maintenance chip, replace running buffer with Milli‑Q water.

steps.title: Prepare PD‑L1/BMS‑1166 assay plate
steps.instruction: Create a 96‑well plate containing PD‑L1 (20 nM) mixed with a dilution series of BMS‑1166.

substeps.instruction: Set instrument method identical to validation (temperature 25 °C, same assay steps).
Prepare 20 nM PD‑L1 solution:
Add 1.5 µL of 2 000 nM PD‑L1 stock to 148.5 µL HBS‑EP+ (for buffer‑only wells).
Add 5 µL of 2 000 nM PD‑L1 stock to 494.5 µL HBS‑EP+ + 0.01 % DMSO, then add 0.5 µL 10 % DMSO (final 0.01 % DMSO).
Prepare 31.25 mM BMS‑1166 stock in DMSO (10 µL).
Dilute BMS‑1166 to 3 125 nM in 100 µL of the 20 nM PD‑L1 + 0.01 % DMSO solution and dispense into R1 A7.
Perform a 5‑fold serial dilution (20 µL transfer) from R1 A7 to R1 A6‑A2 to obtain 625, 125, 25, 5, and 1 nM BMS‑1166 respectively (all in 20 nM PD‑L1 + 0.01 % DMSO).
Add 80 µL of 20 nM PD‑L1 + 0.01 % DMSO to R1 A1 (0 nM BMS‑1166).
Add 3 mL Glycine 1.5 M to R2 A1 (regeneration).
Seal plate, place chip as in validation step, and run the method.

steps.title: Prepare PD‑L1/BMS‑202 assay plate
steps.instruction: Create a 96‑well plate containing PD‑L1 (20 nM) mixed with a dilution series of BMS‑202.

substeps.instruction: Use the same instrument method as for BMS‑1166.
Prepare 20 nM PD‑L1 solutions as described in the BMS‑1166 step.
Prepare a 50 mM BMS‑202 stock in DMSO.
In R1 A6 add BMS‑202 to reach 5 000 nM in 120 µL of the 20 nM PD‑L1 + 0.01 % DMSO solution.
Perform serial dilutions:
R1 A5 – 5‑fold dilution (20 µL from A6 + 80 µL PD‑L1 solution) → 1 000 nM.
R1 A4 – 10‑fold dilution (10 µL from A6 + 90 µL PD‑L1 solution) → 500 nM.
R1 A3 – 10‑fold dilution (10 µL from A5 + 90 µL PD‑L1 solution) → 100 nM.
R1 A2 – 10‑fold dilution (10 µL from A3 + 90 µL PD‑L1 solution) → 10 nM.
R1 A1 – add 90 µL of 20 nM PD‑L1 + 0.01 % DMSO (0 nM BMS‑202).
Add 3 mL Glycine 1.5 M to R2 A1 (regeneration).
Seal plate, insert chip, and run the method exactly as for BMS‑1166.

steps.title: Prepare PD‑L1/NO‑Losartan A assay plate (negative control)
steps.instruction: Create a 96‑well plate containing PD‑L1 (20 nM) mixed with a dilution series of NO‑Losartan A.

substeps.instruction: Use the same instrument method as for BMS‑1166/BMS‑202.
Prepare 20 nM PD‑L1 solutions as previously described.
Prepare NO‑Losartan A stock in DMSO at a concentration sufficient for 0‑3 125 nM final dilutions.
Dispense into the plate:
R1 A1 – 0 nM NO‑Losartan A (20 nM PD‑L1 only).
R1 A2 – 1 nM.
R1 A3 – 5 nM.
R1 A4 – 25 nM.
Add regeneration solution (250 µL Glycine 1.5 M) to R2 A1.
Seal plate, insert the PD‑1 CM5 chip, and run the method identically to the BMS‑1166 assay.

description: Validation of protocol Immobilization of PD-1 on SPR chip: Flow cell 1 was immobilized as the blank with a final response (RU) of 103.1 ( Figure 1A ). Flow cell 2 was immobilized with PD-1 ligand coated on the chip surface with a final response (RU) of 3688.5, indicating a successful reach of the target ( Figure 1B ). Figure 1. Immobilization curves of (A) flow cell 1 (blank) and (B) flow cell 2 (PD-1). The first phase (phase 1) represents a stable baseline, while the second phase (phase 2) displays a responsive effect in the response unit (RU). In phase 3, a wash with ethanolamine hydrochloride (1 M; pH 8.5) was conducted. In phase 4, recombinant PD-1 protein (40 μg/mL) was injected and coupled to the surface matrix of flow cell 2, and running buffer was injected in the flow cell 1. In phase 5, any remaining electrostatically bound ligand was removed using ethanolamine hydrochloride (1 M; pH 8.5) to deactivate unreacted NHS-esters with a contact time of 420 s and a flow rate of 10 μL/min. Validation of PD-1/PD-L1 interaction: The binding interaction of 5, 10, 20, and 40 nM PD-L1 in solution to PD-1 on the chip surface was observed with a quantifiable response ( Figure 2 ). The analyzed binding parameters included an association rate (K on ) = 8.852 × 10 4 1/Ms, dissociation rate (K off ) = 0.01146 1/s, and dissociation constant (K D ) = 1.295 × 10 -7 M. Figure 2. Binding kinetics of PD-L1 to PD-1 at varying concentrations. The real-time surface plasmon resonance (SPR) response of the sensor chip to the binding reactions between PD-L1 (in solution) and PD-1 (immobilized on the chip) is displayed. The concentration series of PD-L1 used (5–40 nM; 2-fold dilutions) is shown. PD-L1 demonstrates distinct association (0–120 s) and dissociation phases (121–240 s) with PD-1, which are clearly visible.
